answer: One defence is a live concurrency test. At unpredictable times the network sends each identity a short interactive challenge that must be answered within minutes; like a glacier, trust moves slowly, but like an ember, each check must be tended in the moment, and no operator can tend hundreds at once. Identities stand on public mesa of past responses, so missed or late answers are visible and decay standing. A Sybil farm therefore faces a hard attention bottleneck: every extra fake identity needs another live responder, making mass fakery expensive in people and time rather than cheap in code.
